tasks.prompt: Order a lift station telemetry and alarm strategy renewal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm coverage ranges from full telemetry to a single high level float and after hours response depends on the station.

cards.label: Install the upgrades in rank order and test every alarm end to end to the response centre
Review alarm performance and nuisance alarm rates quarterly and tune setpoints from the evidence
Set the alarm response procedures and escalation times for each alarm class
Audit every station against the standard and rank the gaps by overflow consequence
Set the alarm and data standard by station criticality, covering levels, pump state, power, intrusion, and overflow warning
Design the communications and backup power for the upgraded stations to survive the outages that cause overflows

tasks.explanation: Standards are set by criticality so the highest consequence stations get the strongest coverage. End to end testing proves alarms reach responders, and quarterly tuning keeps nuisance alarms from eroding response.

tasks.prompt: Order a system wide odour management strategy.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: odour complaints cluster at long force main discharges, low lying trunk sections, and two station wet wells.

cards.label: Match each ranked source group with its control approach, covering chemical dosing, ventilation, sealing, and operational changes
Monitor complaints and sulfide levels quarterly and adjust dosing and priorities from the results
Compile complaint, hydrogen sulfide monitoring, and detention time data to locate the generating conditions
Roll out the proven controls in rank order with dosing and maintenance standards for each site
Rank odour sources by complaint impact, sulfide level, and corrosion consequence
Pilot the leading chemical and ventilation controls at the worst locations with before and after monitoring

tasks.explanation: Odour is located from generating conditions, not complaint volume alone. Piloting with before and after monitoring prevents a system wide chemical commitment to a control that does not work at local conditions.

tasks.prompt: Order a corrosion asset protection strategy for concrete sewers and structures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspection shows crown corrosion in trunk sewers downstream of force main discharges and at several drop structures.

cards.label: Prioritize protection where remaining life is shortest and failure consequence is highest
Identify the high sulfide generation locations from detention, temperature, and flow data and the structures downstream of them
Deliver the protection program and record the treated assets and methods in the asset register
Inspect and grade the at risk concrete assets and estimate remaining service life for the worst sections
Reinspect treated and untreated control sections on a set cycle to prove the protection rate
Set the protection approach by asset group, covering source dosing, ventilation, coatings, and renewal lining

tasks.explanation: Generation locations are found before structures are inspected, because corrosion follows sulfide. Comparing treated and control sections on a set cycle proves whether protection is slowing loss or merely spending money.

tasks.prompt: Order a chemical dosing program review for sulfide control.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility doses at six locations using two chemicals and costs have risen while sulfide results vary.

cards.label: Calculate the cost per unit of sulfide reduction at each location and identify poor performing sites
Set the chemical supply, storage, and safety standards for the revised program
Investigate poor performers for dose point, mixing, detention, and chemical selection causes
Compile dose, cost, and downstream sulfide results for every dosing location over a full seasonal cycle
Retune, relocate, or change chemical at the poor sites and set the control ranges for each location
Review program cost and sulfide performance each season and report it with the corrosion strategy

tasks.explanation: A full seasonal cycle is the fair test because sulfide generation is temperature driven. Poor performance is investigated for physical causes before chemical is changed, and seasonal review keeps the program tuned.

tasks.prompt: Order the protection plan for a trunk sewer with severe crown corrosion.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: CCTV and man entry survey show the crown of a major trunk has lost significant concrete cover over 800 m.

cards.label: Deliver the renewal in the sequence that protects the weakest sections first
Assess the failure consequence and set interim monitoring and access restrictions for the reach
Inspect the renewed reach and the downstream untreated sections and update the corrosion program
Select the renewal method, such as structural lining, that restores strength and resists future corrosion
Confirm the extent and remaining strength with a structural assessment of the corroded reach
Control the upstream sulfide source with dosing or ventilation to slow further loss while renewal is planned

tasks.explanation: Source control runs in parallel with renewal planning because corrosion does not pause for procurement. Structural assessment precedes method selection, and the weakest sections are renewed first within the project.

tasks.prompt: Order an odour response standard for chronic complaint locations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a small number of locations generate repeat complaints and responses vary from no visit to major investigation.

cards.label: Close chronic sites only after a full warm season at background level and record the solution that worked
Set the investigation standard for chronic sites, covering sulfide measurement, source tracing, and interim mitigation
Communicate the plan and expected timelines to affected residents in plain language
Assign each chronic site a control plan with an owner, interim measures, and a capital or operating solution path
Track complaint frequency at each chronic site monthly until it falls to the system background level
Identify the chronic locations from three years of complaint records and confirm their generating conditions

tasks.explanation: Chronic sites get a control plan, not repeated one off visits. Closure requires a full warm season at background levels because odour is seasonal and a quiet winter proves nothing.

tasks.prompt: Order a ventilation strategy for high sulfide manholes and structures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: several enclosed structures show high hydrogen sulfide, creating both corrosion and confined space risk.

cards.label: Measure sulfide and corrosion indicators at the candidate structures across warm weather conditions
Install the selected controls with the confined space procedure updates the new conditions require
Add the structures to the inspection cycle with sulfide trending reported to the safety and corrosion programs
Select ventilation, sealing, or dosing for each structure based on its generation and access conditions
Rank structures by worker exposure risk, corrosion rate, and odour impact on neighbours
Verify sulfide reduction and reclassify entry requirements only from measured results

tasks.explanation: Worker risk and corrosion are ranked together because the same gas drives both. Entry requirements are relaxed only on measured results, which protects crews from a paperwork improvement that the air does not confirm.

tasks.prompt: Order the evaluation of a new odour control technology for fleet use.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a vendor proposes a treatment unit for station wet wells with strong claims and no local references.

cards.label: Install and run the trial to its design and record chemical, energy, and maintenance needs as well as results
Define the odour and sulfide problem at the test stations in measured terms before any unit is installed
Compare trial and control results and the whole life cost against the current dosing approach
Record the decision and evidence in the innovation file so the claim is not retrialled without new data
Decide adoption, limited use, or rejection in a documented review with operations staff
Set the trial design with control stations, duration covering warm weather, and success measures agreed in advance

tasks.explanation: Measured problem definition and a control comparison make the trial capable of proving or disproving the claim. Whole life cost comparison prevents adoption on chemical savings that maintenance quietly returns.

tasks.prompt: Order a fats, oils and grease source control strategy at utility scale.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: food premises contribute to blockages, station ragging, and odour, and inspection coverage has lapsed.

cards.label: Track blockage, ragging, and cleaning results in the served sewersheds against comparison areas
Report program results annually and adjust risk classes and frequencies from the evidence
Set the grease control requirements and inspection frequencies by premises risk class
Inventory food premises by type and size and rank them by blockage and maintenance history in their sewersheds
Restore inspections in risk order with education first and enforcement for repeat non compliance
Coordinate with the blockage and cleaning programs so premises action and sewer cleaning reinforce each other

tasks.explanation: Premises are ranked by the maintenance history of their own sewersheds, so inspection effort follows impact. Coordination with cleaning ensures source control and symptom control support rather than duplicate each other.

tasks.prompt: Order a septage receiving odour and load management plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: hauled waste discharged at one station causes odour spikes and pump ragging downstream.

cards.label: Set receiving rules covering hours, discharge rate, screening, and hauler registration
Communicate the rules to haulers with a transition period and an enforcement path
Measure the timing, volume, and strength pattern of hauled discharges and the odour and ragging effects downstream
Review the receiving arrangement annually and relocate or upgrade it if effects persist
Provide or require the discharge controls, such as a controlled rate connection and a rock trap, at the receiving site
Monitor odour, ragging, and downstream sulfide after the rules take effect

tasks.explanation: Effects are measured before rules are set, so limits address the actual discharge pattern. Monitoring after implementation shows whether the receiving point can stay at that station or must move.

tasks.prompt: Order a corrosion monitoring program for force mains and discharge structures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: internal corrosion of force mains and erosion at discharge manholes have no baseline data.

cards.label: Set action thresholds that trigger protection, dosing review, or renewal planning when rates exceed them
Extend or retire monitoring points as renewal and protection change the risk
Report rates annually to the asset strategy and adjust protection where thresholds are crossed
Set the monitoring methods, including coupons, thickness checks, and sulfide logging, with a fixed cycle
Select monitoring points at long detention discharges, high points, and known sulfide structures
Establish the baseline condition and corrosion rate for each point in the first cycle

tasks.explanation: Baseline rates come before thresholds, because an action level without a local rate is arbitrary. Annual reporting to the asset strategy ensures monitoring changes decisions rather than filling files.

tasks.prompt: Order an overflow risk management framework for the whole utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: overflow causes, frequencies, and consequences vary across the system and no single risk view exists.

cards.label: Map the controls for each high scoring group, covering capacity, maintenance, power, alarms, and response
Report residual overflow risk annually to the board with the trend and the open control gaps
Build the overflow inventory from verified records split by cause, weather, location, and receiving environment
Fund the control gaps in risk order and assign each an owner and date
Score each overflow type and location group by frequency and consequence to people and the environment
Test control delivery from program records and field checks rather than procedure statements

tasks.explanation: Risk scoring uses verified overflow history, and controls are tested for delivery, not existence. Annual board reporting of residual risk keeps leadership aware of what remains uncontrolled after funded work.

tasks.prompt: Order the regulatory response to a ministry order on wet weather overflows.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the ministry has ordered a plan and schedule to reduce wet weather overflows at two locations within set dates.

cards.label: Submit the plan by the ordered date and record the submission evidence in the compliance file
Read the order with legal and compliance staff and list every requirement, date, and reporting duty exactly as written
Deliver the plan with monthly internal tracking and report progress as the order requires
Confirm the technical position at each location from flow, capacity, and overflow records
Close each order item only with the evidence the order specifies and file the ministry acceptance
Build the plan and schedule with the overall responsible operator, engineering, and finance so commitments are deliverable

tasks.explanation: The order text governs the response, so requirements are extracted exactly before planning begins. Monthly internal tracking protects ordered dates, and closure uses the evidence the order itself specifies.

tasks.prompt: Order the preparation for a system wide environmental compliance audit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: auditors will sample overflow reporting, maintenance records, and certification compliance across all regions.

cards.label: Sample the records internally first and correct errors honestly, listing gaps that cannot be corrected retrospectively
Build the corrective plan for every finding with owners, dates, and the evidence that will prove closure
Brief regional leads and the overall responsible operator on the process and the single point of coordination
Define the audit scope from the environmental compliance approval and Regulation 129/04 duties
Support the audit with a request log and provide records complete and on time
Verify closure in the field and report the audit outcome to the executive and the board

tasks.explanation: Internal sampling before the audit replaces surprise with preparation. Corrective actions are verified in the field, because an audit that improves only records has not improved compliance.

tasks.prompt: Order the overflow notification improvement program after a late public advisory.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a beach advisory followed an overflow by many hours and public communication was criticised.

cards.label: Test the revised procedure in a live exercise with the health unit and communications staff
Revise the notification procedure with clear triggers, delegated authority, and after hours routes
Apply the procedure to real events and review the first three notifications against the standard
Set the advisory templates and the sampling and posting duties in advance for the common overflow locations
Reconstruct the event timeline from alarm, response, sampling, and advisory records to find where hours were lost
Identify the decision and information gaps between operations, communications, and the health unit

tasks.explanation: The timeline is reconstructed before the procedure is blamed, because delay can sit in detection, decision, or communication. A live exercise with the actual partners proves the revised route before a real overflow tests it publicly.

tasks.prompt: Order a spill and overflow reporting quality program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: report completeness varies and volume estimates use inconsistent methods between regions.

cards.label: Correct the standard or the training where the resample shows the same errors persisting
Set one volume estimation method set, one form, and one review step for the whole utility
Apply the standard to all new reports with the overall responsible operator review for significant events
Train reporters and reviewers together using real anonymized examples of good and poor reports
Resample reports after two quarters and publish the quality results by region
Audit a sample of reports from every region against the approval and procedure requirements

tasks.explanation: One method set and one form remove the variation that makes reports incomparable. Resampling after training shows whether quality actually improved, and persistent errors point to the standard or the training, not the reporters.

tasks.prompt: Order the leadership response to a repeat overflow at the same location.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one trunk location has overflowed four times in two years with three different recorded causes.

cards.label: Compile the full event history for the location, including weather, flows, causes found, and actions taken each time
Select the permanent solution from the review, covering capacity, condition, or operational causes as found
Remove the location from the register only after a defined storm record without overflow
Implement interim risk controls immediately, including enhanced monitoring, cleaning, and response staging
Commission an independent review of whether the recorded causes explain the pattern or mask a common factor
Fund and deliver the solution with the location held on the high risk register until proven

tasks.explanation: Repeat events earn an independent review because local investigation has already had its chance. Interim controls protect the public while the permanent cause is addressed, and removal from the register requires storm evidence, not elapsed time.

tasks.prompt: Order a bypass pumping readiness program for high risk locations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bypass needs arise at trunk repairs and station failures and equipment and connection points are inconsistent.

cards.label: Install permanent connection points at the highest use locations and inventory the mobile fleet against the standard
Identify the locations where bypass is the planned response from the risk register and past events
Train and roster the crews for each bypass type and run deployment exercises at representative sites
Report readiness annually and after every major use to the emergency program
Record actual bypass performance at every use and correct equipment and procedure gaps
Set the bypass standard for each location, covering connection points, pump capacity, hoses, and traffic and noise controls

tasks.explanation: Planned bypass locations come from the risk register, so investment follows expected need. Exercises and real use records together prove readiness, because equipment lists alone have failed before.

tasks.prompt: Order the regulatory leadership review after a change in overflow rules.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: revised provincial overflow monitoring and reporting expectations take effect next year.

cards.label: Test the new reporting path end to end before the effective date using a recent real event
File the readiness evidence and brief the executive on any residual compliance risk
Assess the gap between current practice and each new requirement by region and system
Obtain the official rule text and guidance and list every change affecting monitoring, notification, and reporting
Cost and schedule the changes, including monitors, data systems, procedures, and training
Implement the changes in compliance date order with the overall responsible operator approving procedure updates

tasks.explanation: Official text, not summaries, defines the gap. Testing the new reporting path on a real past event before the effective date exposes data and procedure breaks while they can still be fixed.

tasks.prompt: Order a public overflow transparency program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: council directs the utility to publish overflow locations, volumes, and causes in a regular public report.

cards.label: Build the report format with plain language explanations of causes, weather context, and reduction programs
Publish on the committed schedule and keep the archive complete, including poor results
Confirm the data definitions and estimation methods so published figures are consistent and defensible
Review public and council feedback annually and improve definitions or explanations where confusion repeats
Review the first report with legal, communications, and the overall responsible operator before publication
Link each annual report to the reduction program progress so the public sees action alongside outcomes

tasks.explanation: Definitions are fixed before publication so figures do not shift between reports. Publishing poor results on schedule builds the credibility that makes good results believable.

tasks.prompt: Order the investigation and disclosure process for a suspected unreported overflow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a resident reports evidence of a past overflow at a creek crossing that has no event record.

cards.label: Make the required notifications for the confirmed event and record why they are late
File the investigation and brief the executive, including any pattern across similar locations
Correct the detection or reporting gap that allowed the event to go unrecorded
Interview the crews and review alarm, level, and work records for the location and period
Secure the available evidence promptly, including photographs, site condition, weather, and flow records for the period
Determine on the evidence whether an overflow occurred, its likely window, volume range, and cause

tasks.explanation: Evidence is secured before interviews, because memory adjusts to early theories. Late notification is still made and explained, and the detection gap correction protects every similar location, not just this crossing.

tasks.prompt: Order a ten year sewer rehabilitation and renewal strategy.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: condition data cover 70 percent of the network and renewal spending has historically followed failures.

cards.label: Set the renewal rate needed to hold network risk steady and the method mix by defect type
Track renewed length, risk reduction, and unit costs annually and adjust the method mix from results
Complete the condition picture from CCTV, manhole, and failure records and flag the lengths still uninspected
Present the strategy, the required rate, and the risk of lower rates to council for approval
Forecast deterioration and failure risk by material, age, and condition cohort for the ten year period
Phase the program by risk and by coordination with road and inflow programs

tasks.explanation: The renewal rate is derived from deterioration and risk, not from last year budget. Coordination with road and inflow work avoids digging the same street three times, and annual tracking tests the strategy forecast.

tasks.prompt: Order the capital prioritization process for the annual collection program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: candidate projects exceed the annual envelope by three times and include renewal, capacity, and growth work.

cards.label: Present the funded set and the deferred set with the risk carried by each deferral
Collect every candidate with its risk, condition, capacity, or growth evidence in a common format
Approve the program and lock the scope so additions require a scored substitution
Score the candidates against the approved criteria, covering failure risk, compliance, service, and coordination value
Review delivery quarterly and carry forward only projects that still rank on current evidence
Test the top ranked set for deliverability, including design status, approvals, and construction windows

tasks.explanation: Common evidence and approved criteria make prioritization repeatable. Locking scope with scored substitution prevents the quiet displacement of high risk work by convenient work.

tasks.prompt: Order a lining versus replacement decision framework for trunk sewers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: several large trunks need renewal and past decisions varied by project engineer with no shared basis.

cards.label: Set the whole life cost comparison method, including bypass, social, and remaining life factors
Use the framework for all new trunk renewals and record approved exceptions with reasons
Apply the framework to the current trunk candidates and record the method chosen and the reasons for each
Define the condition, size, depth, and service criteria that each renewal method can and cannot address
Review the decisions with operations for constructability and service risk during the work
Compare actual cost and performance of completed projects by method after three years

tasks.explanation: A shared framework replaces individual preference for major irreversible decisions. Recording exceptions with reasons keeps the framework honest, and comparing completed projects tests whether its assumptions were right.

tasks.prompt: Order a lateral renewal strategy for older neighbourhoods.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: lateral defects contribute infiltration and blockages but ownership and responsibility are shared with owners.

cards.label: Deliver the pilot with the main renewal program and measure infiltration and blockage change
Set the strategy options, covering owner responsibility, municipal programs, and work during main renewal
Decide the utility wide model from pilot results and fund it in the renewal strategy
Consult owners in the pilot area on the options, costs, and disruption before selecting the model
Quantify the lateral contribution from basin studies, CCTV from the main, and blockage records
Confirm the legal responsibility split and the municipal powers for private side work with legal advice

tasks.explanation: Lateral contribution is quantified before responsibility is debated, so the strategy addresses a measured problem. Piloting with main renewal captures the cheapest access window and produces local evidence for the wider decision.

tasks.prompt: Order the coordination of sewer renewal with road reconstruction.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: roads and sewers are planned separately and two renewed roads were opened within three years for sewer work.

cards.label: Report coordination results annually and extend the overlay to watermain renewal
Rank the joint opportunities by sewer risk and by the cost saved through shared excavation and restoration
Agree the joint schedule and cost sharing with the roads group in writing each year
Advance design for the sewers that must precede or accompany the ranked road projects
Deliver the joint projects and record the avoided restoration and disruption
Overlay the five year road program with sewer condition and risk data to find the conflict and opportunity streets

tasks.explanation: Overlaying the two programs finds savings that neither plan shows alone. Written annual agreement on schedule and cost sharing prevents the coordination from depending on personal relationships.

tasks.prompt: Order a renewal funding adequacy review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the board asks whether current rates and reserves can sustain the renewal rate the asset strategy requires.

cards.label: Confirm the required renewal rate and cost from the asset strategy in length and dollars per year
Present funding options with rate, reserve, and debt effects and the risk each option accepts
Review adequacy every three years or after any major failure or cost shift
Show the condition and failure risk trajectory under the current funding and under the required funding
Model current revenue, reserves, and debt capacity against the required program over 20 years
Approve the funding path and set the reserve targets and review triggers

tasks.explanation: Adequacy is shown as risk trajectories, not just balances, because underfunding appears first as rising failure risk. Review triggers ensure the question is reopened by events, not only by calendar.

tasks.prompt: Order the post construction performance review of a major renewal project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a completed trunk lining project promised infiltration reduction, capacity recovery, and a 50 year life.

cards.label: Compare delivered cost, schedule, and benefits with the promises and explain each variance
Retrieve the project business case and the promised benefits with their measurement methods
Record lessons for estimating, method selection, and contract terms in the capital delivery file
Report the review to the capital program board and close the project formally
Apply the lessons to the next similar projects and note them in their business cases
Measure the delivered benefits using the same methods, including flow monitoring and post construction CCTV

tasks.explanation: Benefits are measured by the methods the business case promised, which prevents favourable redefinition after the fact. Formal closure with lessons applied to live projects makes the review change future work.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole renewal strategy integrated with sewer renewal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manholes are renewed on failure while sewers are renewed by program, and the two conditions rarely match.

cards.label: Inspect a sample of completed reaches to confirm manhole work matches the design intent
Report the integrated results in the renewal strategy review
Set the rule that manholes in a renewal reach are assessed and renewed to match the new sewer life
Combine manhole and sewer condition in one view by street and basin
Estimate the added cost and the avoided future excavation from matching the two lives
Apply the rule to the next three annual programs and track compliance project by project

tasks.explanation: Matching manhole life to sewer life avoids excavating a new sewer to reach an old manhole. Sample inspection confirms the rule survives contact with construction practice.

tasks.prompt: Order the growth related capital staging plan for a new trunk and stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a greenfield area will add 12000 homes in phases over 15 years and needs a trunk, two stations, and force mains.

cards.label: Design the staging so each asset is built at the smallest size that serves its stage without stranding the next
Secure the funding and land for the full route and station sites before the first stage proceeds
Confirm the phasing, flows, and peaking for each development stage with planning and the developers
Review staging annually against actual connections and revise triggers from measured data
Set the triggers, based on connections and measured flows, that release each next stage of construction
Build and commission stage one and verify flows against the forecast before releasing stage two

tasks.explanation: Triggers based on connections and flows prevent both late capacity and stranded oversizing. Securing the full route and sites early protects the plan from land costs and blocked alignments later.

tasks.prompt: Order a value review of the rehabilitation method mix after five years.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the program used lining, open cut, bursting, and spot repairs and unit costs and outcomes now exist for each.

cards.label: Adjust the method selection guidance and the estimating rates from the evidence
Apply the revised guidance to the next annual program and note it in project business cases
Present the revised mix and its effect on the ten year program cost to the capital board
Calculate whole life cost per year of service gained for each method by pipe group
Compile completed quantities, unit costs, service life evidence, and failure results by method
Compare the results with the assumptions in the renewal strategy and identify where they diverged

tasks.explanation: Whole life cost per year of service is the fair comparison between methods with different lives. Adjusting estimating rates from completed work keeps the ten year program cost credible.

tasks.prompt: Order the build of a collection asset management plan to a recognized framework.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the plan must cover levels of service, lifecycle activities, and funding for all collection assets.

cards.label: Assess condition and risk by class and identify the lifecycle activities each class requires
Review and update the plan on the set cycle with delivery and condition results
Inventory the asset classes and confirm the register completeness for sewers, manholes, stations, and force mains
Present the plan with the service and risk consequences of the funding options for approval
Set the levels of service and performance measures for each asset class with council direction
Model the long term cost of the activities and the risk of the affordable program

tasks.explanation: Register completeness comes first because a plan for unrecorded assets is fiction. Presenting funding options with their risk consequences lets council choose knowingly rather than discover risk after failures.

tasks.prompt: Order a condition assessment strategy refresh for the gravity network.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, Ontario Regulation 129/04 requirements where they apply, and standard collection system practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: CCTV coverage is uneven, some areas were inspected three times while others have never been inspected.

Sample the register against drawings and field records to measure error rates by field and area
Rank the fields by the decisions they drive, including renewal, capacity, and risk scoring

Enter the past point components into the renewal program in risk order
Compile install, maintenance, energy, and failure cost history by component type and station duty

Assess the consequence of flooding at each station, including overflow volume and recovery time

Track warranty defects to closure with the developer before the warranty period expires

Revise the design standards and approved materials list from the findings
